Doing good work isn't enough to get you promoted, saysRyan Peterman, an engineer atMeta. You also have to make sure everyone knows about it."If you go and build this amazing feature that nobody knows about, it doesn't matter how good it is, you're not going to get any recognition for it," Peterman said during a talk at UCLA. "And so, how do you advocate for yourself after you've done great work, which is the hard part?"Making your accomplishments as public as possible is the key "last few percent" of climbing the career ladder, Peterman said.
